job.title: Health & Safety Advisor - Technical, Systems and Content
job.description:
Join a respected consultancy shaping safety across Australia and New Zealand. 
We are partnering with a highly regarded workplace health and safety consultancy to recruit a Health and Safety Advisor for their Sydney based team. This is an opportunity to step into a role with genuine influence, where your work will shape safety standards for organisations across Australia and New Zealand.

If you enjoy technical writing, systems, problem solving, and turning complex legislation into practical, usable guidance, this role offers the perfect blend of creativity, impact, and professional growth.

About the Role
As a Health and Safety Advisor, you will sit within a specialist team that develops the safety materials used by internal teams and clients nationally. Your work will directly contribute to safer workplaces by creating clear, compliant, and engaging documentation that people can easily understand and apply.
You will collaborate with subject matter experts, support capability building across the business, and occasionally contribute to seminars, webinars, and training initiatives. No two days will look the same, and you will have the chance to take ownership of meaningful, high profile content.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Creating and updating workplace health and safety policies, manuals, procedures, and supporting documents
  • Reviewing legislation and providing practical, actionable guidance
  • Responding to complex internal queries and offering expert technical advice
  • Contributing to training and communication content, including presentations and workshops
  • Supporting audits and inspections of safety systems where required
  • Presenting technical information in a clear, engaging, and client friendly way
About You
  • Certificate IV in WHS minimum, Diploma preferred
  • At least three years workplace health and safety experience
  • Strong written communication and technical writing ability
  • Confident engaging with internal stakeholders
  • Current understanding of Australian WHS legislation
  • Proactive, detail focused, and solutions oriented
What is on Offer
  • Office based role in central Sydney
  • Supportive and collaborative team culture
  • Opportunities to influence safety content nationally
If you enjoy technical safety work and want to make a broader impact, we would love to hear from you.
 
Apply in the links or enquire via email to Stephen Coldicutt scoldicutt@thesafestep.com.au

job.title: Head of Safety
job.description:

With a strong pipeline of work and significant growth ahead, the organisation is seeking a strategic yet hands-on Head of Safety to help build the systems, capability and culture required to support the next stage of its journey.

This is a business that moves quickly. As projects grow in scale and complexity, you will need to balance safety excellence with operational delivery, influencing stakeholders to maintain high standards while enabling the organisation to continue performing at pace.

Key Priorities
  • Build and implement a scalable safety strategy aligned to significant business growth.
  • Further embed a proactive safety culture where safety is a visible and valued part of day-to-day operations.
  • Strengthen systems, governance, reporting and leading indicators to support informed decision-making.
  • Drive greater ownership of safety across the business and influence leaders at all levels.
  • Lead initiatives across physical safety, psychosocial risk and wellbeing. 
  • Ensure the safety function can support a rapidly growing workforce and project portfolio.
About You

You are an experienced safety executive who knows how to build capability and drive change in dynamic project environments. You are comfortable operating with ambiguity, making decisions quickly and influencing stakeholders across executive, operational and frontline levels. 
You will bring:
  • Senior safety leadership experience within construction, electrical, infrastructure, utilities or major projects.
  • A track record of building scalable safety frameworks in growing organisations
  • Strong commercial acumen and the ability to balance safety, productivity and delivery outcomes.
  • Exceptional stakeholder engagement and influencing skills.
  • The resilience and agility to succeed in a business undergoing rapid transformation and growth.
Why This Role?

This is a genuine opportunity to put your stamp on an organisation at a pivotal stage of growth. You'll have the autonomy, executive support and resources to build a contemporary safety function, influence business strategy and help shape the culture of a company delivering some of the country's most significant data centre and critical infrastructure projects.

If you're energised by growth, enjoy working at pace and want the opportunity to build something meaningful rather than simply maintain it, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Safety and Compliance Manager
job.description:
About the company

Join a leading Australian security and safety services organisation with a strong national footprint and an ambition to be recognised as a market leader across the industry.
Built around the values of Transparency, Inclusiveness and Excellence, the organisation is continuing to strengthen its approach to workplace health, safety, risk and compliance. This is an opportunity to take ownership of the safety agenda across a diverse Australian workforce and play a key role in embedding a genuine safety-first culture across the business.
With operations spanning multiple locations and business functions, the organisation is looking for a safety leader who can combine strategic thinking with practical operational engagement and influence.

About the role

Reporting to the HR Manager, the Safety & Compliance Manager will lead the development and implementation of the organisation's national WHS, risk and compliance framework.
This is a highly visible role, requiring someone who can work closely with executives, senior leaders, managers and frontline teams to turn safety strategy into everyday behaviours and outcomes.
A key focus will be building leadership capability through national face-to-face training, coaching and engagement, supported by regular site visits, safety observations and operational reviews. You will challenge and influence leaders to take genuine ownership of safety within their teams while ensuring consistent standards across the organisation.
You will oversee WHS systems, risk assessments, incident investigations, audits, corrective actions, workers' compensation and return-to-work processes, while maintaining alignment with Australian legislation and the organisation's ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 management systems.
You will also provide meaningful reporting and insights to senior leadership, identifying emerging risks, trends and opportunities for continuous improvement.

About you

You are an experienced WHS, safety, risk or compliance professional who is equally comfortable developing strategy and getting onto the ground to make it happen.
You will bring strong knowledge of Australian WHS legislation and regulatory frameworks, together with a proven ability to influence leadership behaviour and drive cultural change across diverse workforces.
Your strength will be your ability to engage people at all levels. You can coach a senior manager, challenge an operational leader and connect with frontline employees in a way that creates ownership rather than simply compliance.
Strong communication, stakeholder management and influencing skills are essential, as is the ability to analyse safety performance and translate information into practical action.
A tertiary qualification in WHS, Risk Management or a related discipline is preferred, along with experience working across multiple sites or locations.
National travel will be required.

For a confidential conversation, please contact Jon Hottot at the Safe Step on 0488 420003 or jhottot@thesafestep.com.au

job.title: Health, Safety & Wellbeing Advisor
job.description:
Health, Safety & Wellbeing Advisor
  
Eastern Seaboard | Sydney-based on-site Monday-Friday | Nationally growing business
  
Build credibility. Shape strategy. Make a genuine impact.
  
A newly created opportunity has arisen for a practical and relationship-focused Health, Safety & Wellbeing Advisor to join a rapidly growing national construction materials business undergoing a significant safety transformation.
  
With strong executive commitment to safety and investment in additional capability, this is an opportunity to play a foundational role in shaping the next phase of the organisation's safety journey.
  
This is not a traditional compliance-focused Safety Advisor role. The priority is to be visible across the operation, build trusted relationships and understand how work is actually performed.
  
The Role
Supporting operations across the Eastern Seaboard, you will act as the eyes and ears of the safety function, spending approximately 80% of your time in the field.
  
Your focus will include:
  • Building strong relationships with operational leaders and frontline teams
  • Understanding operational risks and the realities of work "as done"
  • Providing practical safety advice and support
  • Identifying emerging risks, trends and opportunities for improvement
  • Supporting incident investigations and organisational learning
  • Conducting field-based assurance and verification activities
  • Improving safety systems, reporting, processes and documentation
  • Contributing to the development of a comprehensive operational risk profile
  • Supporting the broader uplift in safety maturity across the business
  
The operating environment includes transport, logistics, equipment, mobile plant and field-based activities, so practical operational experience is important.
  
About You
You will be an experienced Safety Advisor who enjoys being close to operations and building genuine relationships with people at all levels.
  
Experience in transport, logistics, construction, manufacturing, industrial operations, heavy industry, mining or mobile plant environments would be highly relevant.
  
You will bring:
  • Practical WHS and risk management experience
  • Experience supporting incident investigations
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills
  • A curious, collaborative and solutions-focused approach
  • The confidence to challenge respectfully and influence without authority
  • The ability to work autonomously across multiple sites
  • A genuine willingness to travel across Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and regional Queensland as required
  
Experience in injury management, return to work, workers' compensation or assurance would be advantageous, but is not essential.
  
Why Join?
This is an opportunity to join a business with genuine appetite for change and improvement, where safety has strong senior leadership support.
  
You will have the opportunity to:
  • Make a visible and meaningful impact
  • Help shape the future safety strategy
  • Build strong relationships across a growing national operation
  • Work closely with senior safety leadership
  • Develop broad operational exposure
  • Position yourself for future leadership opportunities as the Eastern Seaboard safety function grows
  
If you're a practical safety professional who believes the best safety outcomes come from working with people, not policing them, we'd like to hear from you.
  
About Applying
At TSS, we embrace individuality and differences in gender, age, ethnicity, race, cultural background, disability, faith and sexual orientation. We strive to provide a recruitment experience that’s fair, inclusive and accessible. We encourage all suitable applicants to apply for this role.
For any accessibility needs to be considered during the recruitment process, please let us know at support@thesafestep.com.au
                       
For a confidential discussion, please contact John Spring at jspring@thesafestep.com.au or click “Apply” to apply for this role.

job.title: Head of Health, Safety & Wellbeing

  • Leading the delivery of Casey's Health, Safety & Wellbeing strategy.
  • Strengthening safety governance, assurance and compliance frameworks.

job.title: Head of HSE Operations
job.description:
HEAD OF HSEQ OPERATIONS

National Executive Safety Leadership Opportunity (based in Brisbane/Sydney or Melbourne)

ABOUT THE COMPANY

An established and nationally recognised Australian transport organisation is seeking an experienced safety leader to join its senior leadership team.
Operating across multiple jurisdictions, the organisation delivers essential public services through a geographically dispersed workforce and complex, high-risk operational environments. Safety is fundamental to its success, and the business has established a strong safety culture and industry-leading safety outcomes relative to its peer group.

Continued growth, the integration of new operations and increasing complexity across the risk landscape have created an opportunity for a senior safety professional to influence safety performance at a national level.
This is also an organisation that invests in its people, with genuine succession pathways and opportunities for high-performing leaders to progress into broader executive roles.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Reporting directly to the General Manager HSEQ, the Head of HSEQ Operations is a pivotal national leadership position responsible for driving consistency, capability, governance and continual improvement across the organisation.

This is not a desk-bound corporate safety role. The successful candidate will combine strategic thinking with strong operational credibility, working closely with Managing Directors, operational leaders and regional safety teams to identify emerging risks and deliver practical improvements.
Key responsibilities will include:
  • Analyse safety data, trends and leading indicators to identify emerging and high-consequence risks.
  • Develop and implement national safety improvement initiatives.
  • Strengthen consistency across safety systems, processes and standards.
  • Lead and support major incident and ICAM investigations, ensuring organisational learning is embedded.
  • Provide assurance across integrated management systems, ISO frameworks, compliance and audit programs.
  • Consolidate and interpret national safety data to provide meaningful insight to Executive and Board stakeholders.
  • Mentor and develop regional safety leaders and build safety capability across the organisation.
  • Partner with operational leaders to deliver sustainable improvements while balancing governance with commercial and operational realities.
The role has significant national influence, including a dotted-line leadership relationship with regional safety professionals across multiple operating divisions.

ABOUT YOU

You will be an experienced safety leader who is comfortable operating in complex, high-risk and geographically dispersed environments.
You are likely to bring:
  • Significant senior HSEQ leadership experience across transport, rail, logistics, infrastructure, construction, mining, manufacturing or another comparable high-risk industry.
  • Strong operational risk management capability, ideally including heavy vehicle or transport-related risk.
  • Experience with ISO-certified management systems, audit and assurance.
  • Proven ICAM and serious incident investigation capability.
  • Experience working across multiple sites, jurisdictions and diverse operational cultures.
  • Strong analytical capability, with the ability to turn safety data into meaningful business insight.
  • The credibility to influence senior executives while remaining connected to frontline operations.
Most importantly, you will be a practical, collaborative and emotionally mature leader who builds relationships before implementing change.
You will be confident challenging constructively, comfortable operating under pressure and capable of influencing without relying on authority. You will understand that effective safety leadership is ultimately about earning trust, building capability and helping operational leaders achieve better outcomes.
This is an exceptional opportunity for a senior safety professional who wants to move beyond functional leadership and make a genuine national impact, while positioning themselves for future broader executive leadership opportunities.

job.title: Director, Safety I VicGrid
job.description:
Join VicGrid and help shape the safety culture behind Victoria's next generation of energy infrastructure.

Location options: Melbourne or Regional Victoria

The Safe Step is proud to be partnering with VicGrid in seeking an accomplished Director, Safety to provide strategic and operational health and safety leadership across its Renewable Energy Zone (REZ) developments and broader portfolio of major energy infrastructure projects.

About VicGrid
VicGrid is a Victorian State Business Corporation responsible for planning Victoria’s transmission network and Renewable Energy Zones as the state transitions towards renewable energy. VicGrid is taking a coordinated approach to developing the transmission infrastructure Victoria needs to maintain a reliable and affordable electricity supply as ageing coal-fired generation retires.

The scale and complexity of VicGrid’s work is substantial.  Its current portfolio of projects will play an important role in reshaping Victoria's energy network and represent some of the state's most significant current and future infrastructure investment.

About the Opportunity
As Director, Safety and a member of the VicGrid Leadership Team, you will lead VicGrid's health and safety function and develop a high-performing Safety team, supporting the safe development and delivery of its programs. You will play a critical role in embedding safety into project planning and delivery while driving a positive, proactive and industry-leading safety culture.

You will lead the implementation of VicGrid's safety strategy, project risk and assurance activities and contractor safety frameworks, while providing trusted advice to Program Directors and senior leaders across the organisation.

Working across a complex stakeholder environment, you will have the opportunity to shape safety standards, behaviours and practices across VicGrid's project portfolio and the broader industry.

About you
You will be a highly experienced safety leader with a strong track record working across major infrastructure/construction, energy, utilities or similarly complex project environments.

You will combine deep technical safety expertise with the leadership presence and influencing capability required to operate effectively with executives, senior project leaders, contractors, regulators and government stakeholders.

Experience working within an active client model, with the ability to effectively influence delivery partners, provide appropriate governance and assurance, and navigate the balance between oversight and contractor accountability, is highly regarded.

You will bring:
  • A credible and pragmatic safety leadership approach, with strong executive presence balanced with humility, curiosity and authenticity.
  • The ability to connect with diverse teams and stakeholders, harness existing capability and bring people with you.
  • High levels of judgement, with the ability to prioritise and move comfortably between hands-on delivery, strategic thinking and senior-level influence.
  • Experience driving cultural change through safety initiatives and programs.
  • Strong leadership capability, with demonstrated experience developing high-performing teams.
  • The ability to provide strategic advice and constructive challenge at executive and senior project leadership level.
  • Strong project and risk management capability within complex, high-profile delivery environments.
  • The ability to lead and navigate significant organisational and industry change.
Why join VicGrid?
The 2025 Victorian Transmission Plan sets out a long-term, coordinated approach to the development of Victoria's energy infrastructure network. As VicGrid continues to lead planning, coordination and delivery across a significant portfolio of energy infrastructure initiatives, this role offers a unique opportunity to influence how major projects are safely developed and delivered across the state.

As Director, Safety, you will provide strategic leadership during a pivotal period for Victoria's energy transition, embedding a safety-first culture and establishing the frameworks, governance and capability that will support the successful delivery of VicGrid's objectives for years to come.
